articles.title: How Bayern Munich fell in love with Kane
articles.summary: It was approaching midnight when Harry Kane emerged to take the congratulations of the media patiently waiting for a word with Bayern Munich's new Ballon d'Or winner. He had not even played in their 6-1 cup win over Magdeburg but it still felt like his night.
body: Harry Kane made a hero's return to the Allianz Arena for Bayern Munich's game against Magdeburg and was saluted by his teammates and fans. With insight from the legendary Lothar Matthaus, Adam Bate reports from Munich on Kane's Bayern romance...

He joked about his children playing with the trophy. He responded to calls for him to be knighted: "I would feel weird if everyone called me Sir." Bizarrely, he even faced questions about being given a golden schnitzel: "I saw that one more as a trophy than to eat it."

Kane insists that he was ready to play but it is clear that what he refers to himself as "a big emotional load" has had an impact on him. "It feels like the Freiburg game was six weeks ago," he said. In reality, it was Sunday. "So much has happened in the last 48 hours."

Naturally, much of the focus since has been on him becoming only the fifth Englishman to claim this award and the first in a quarter of a century. But Bayern have waited two decades longer than that to see one of their own claim this prize. They adore Kane.

He had not even played in their 6-1 cup win over Magdeburg but it still felt like his night.

articles.title: Everybody hates Pat: is a cabal of college kids really trying to bring down ESPN’s star meathead?
articles.summary: Pat McAfee’s reaction to a few mild jokes shows how the ubiquitous ESPN personality is happy to whip up a crowd into a hostile frenzy but is terrified of any criticism. It was all shaping up to be a golden year for Pat McAfee.
body: Then, over the weekend, disaster struck. A handful of college kids attacked him online ahead of his appearance with College GameDay at the University of Utah. Well, “attacked” is maybe overstating things: they made a few mild jokes at his expense. But it was all too much for ESPN’s brightest blimp. Suddenly, McAfee’s world came crashing down. His initial reaction, to be fair, was mild: “The university’s Instagram account posted something talking a little trash about me last night, which I certainly love,” he said ahead of the Utes’ clash with the Houston Cougars last week.

But by Monday the narrative had changed. On his eponymous show, McAfee said he had “never felt more uncomfortable” than he did on the Utah campus, alluding to the assassination of Charlie Kirk as a reason for his unease: “I thought to myself: Has anything really scary happened at, like, a college gathering in the state of Utah recently? Do you think we should be amplifying reasons for why people hate my guts as a university? I don’t know.”

articles.title: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down
articles.summary: From Ms Rachel to Roc Nation, the internet embraced a Florida toddler. Police records reviewed by the Guardian complicate the story – and raise troubling questions. There is real tragedy in this week’s story of the three-year-old Florida boy whose parents claimed he was so good at soccer that…
body: You may have seen the video by now. Here was a toddler with fabulous soccer talent, running end-to-end and scoring goal after goal against opponents who have seemingly just found their feet. The cameraman, later identified as the child’s father, loudly and proudly cheers his son on. Way to go, kid.

Then, an abrupt cut to the parents speaking with two police officers from the Orlando suburb of Winter Park. “They called the police on a three-year-old, because he’s too good,” one of the parents says. An officer responds: “They’re wanting you guys to head out, OK?” The parents ask: “You’re confused too, right?”

In the final shot, his mother says: “This is the biggest part of it. We’re trying to put a show on in front of these people. It’s all on [TikTok] Live. There’s thousands of people watching this. He’s famous. There’s thousands of people watching this.”
points: From Ms Rachel to Roc Nation, the internet embraced a Florida toddler.
Police records reviewed by the Guardian complicate the story – and raise troubling questions.
Here was a toddler with fabulous soccer talent, running end-to-end and scoring goal after goal against opponents who have seemingly just found their feet.

body: English football trailblazer Dilan Markanday has told Sky Sports News he is 'a hundred per cent' interested in playing for the Indian national team.

In-form Chesterfield winger Markanday is a proud British-Indian, who last week celebrated five years since becoming the first British South Asian to play for Tottenham Hotspur in 140 years of the club's history.
But legislative requirements mean Indian diaspora and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs) are only able to represent the nation if they surrender their overseas passport and take up Indian citizenship.

articles.title: WNBA Finals set to make history: Watch Game 6 live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: On Thursday, either the Golden State Valkyries will win a WNBA championship in just their second year of existence, live on Sky Sports, or the Atlanta Dream will force the first Game 7 in league history.
body: Amid scheduling drama, which has resulted in a 12.30pm tip off time in Atlanta - and 9.30am in San Francisco - the match is still a sell out and much anticipated.
"I'd like to see it be a national holiday for all WNBA championship games," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said in jest this week.

"I hope everybody gets to see it, somehow. I know for some people, it's not realistic. They have jobs. They won't be able to make it. I'm disappointed for that, but I'm really hopeful that as many people can see the game as possible."
The game could have been played at Atlanta's 'usual' home court at the Gateway Center Arena on Thursday night. It would have been a great atmosphere, but nobody wanted the tiny crowd of 3,500 or so.

articles.title: Do Dundee United have Scotland's best midfield three?
articles.summary: As Dundee United hold reigning champions Celtic to a draw in Glasgow, the question is posed about whether they have the best midfield in Scotland.
body: Do Dundee United have the best midfield three in the Scottish Premiership? With a man called Zidane at the heart of it all?
That was the question being posed after Jim Goodwin's side stretched their unbeaten run to six games with a hard-earned 2-2 draw that prevented Celtic stretching their lead at the top of the table.

United have slipped to fifth thanks to city rivals Dundee's 3-1 victory over Kilmarnock, and Irishman Goodwin was left disappointed his side had failed to win at Celtic Park for the first time in 52 games stretching back to 1992.
But Goodwin, Celtic counterpart Martin O'Neill and the BBC pundits were full of praise for how they gave the reigning champions a fright and continue to impress.

articles.title: Mourinho and chaos - is Real Madrid boss misunderstood?
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has spent the past decade seeing other managers hailed as geniuses, but did Real Madrid's win at Barcelona show he's been misunderstood?
body: Barcelona fans have long teased Jose Mourinho, with their insult of choice being traductor - Spanish for translator.
It is their way of mocking the Real Madrid manager's humble beginnings.
Learning his future trade while serving as an interpreter for the legendary Sir Bobby Robson, Mourinho followed Robson from Sporting to Porto, before the pair reached Barcelona in 1996.
Four years later Mourinho was the manager of Benfica, the first steps in a coaching career that would lead him to Champions League glory, twice, and success in England, Italy and Spain.

articles.title: Brewers win first World Series in 57-year history
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers win the World Series for the first time in the franchise's 57-year history after beating the Tampa Bay Rays in game five on Wednesday.
body: The Milwaukee Brewers have won the World Series for the first time in the franchise's 57-year history.
They beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in game five in Florida on Wednesday to clinch a 4-1 win in the best-of-seven Fall Classic.
The Brewers, whose only previous appearance in the World Series came in 1982, are based in Major League Baseball's smallest market and this year had the 19th highest payroll of its 30 teams.
But for the second straight year, the Brewers finished the regular season with MLB's best record and they then proved their class with a dominant run in the play-offs.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso is facing his first Chelsea crisis and it could lead to the unthinkable
articles.summary: IN FOCUS: Hailed as Chelsea’s next great entertainer six months ago, Estevao is facing an uncertain future under Xabi Alonso, who faced dissent from supporters at Anfield after leaving the exciting Brazilian on the bench. By Richard Jolly
body: There could have been a few flashbacks to the past for Xabi Alonso. A return to Anfield brought back some of the hostility and the chants from the mid-2000s, when Jose Mourinho and Rafa Benitez patrolled the technical areas, seeking to micromanage everything. Yet some of the issues the new Chelsea manager is experiencing have echoes of problems he encountered – some would say created – at Real Madrid.

Then a Brazilian teenager seemed to be marginalised by his manager. Then a Brazilian winger seemed unhappy with his manager. For both Endrick and Vinicius Junior at the Bernabeu, read Estevao at Stamford Bridge?

It can seem so, despite Alonso’s calm, matter-of-fact answers. “I understand his situation and that he could be happier, for sure,” he said. “Every player wants to play, wants to be part of the team.”

But Estevao has not been. Chelsea were knocked out of the Carabao Cup without him playing a minute in Wednesday’s loss to Liverpool. He has played a mere 47 minutes in the Premier League, an 18-minute outing against Tottenham on Saturday coming after cameos of seven, nine, four, three and six respectively.

With the quarter-final draw being made shortly after the match at Anfield ended last night, Iraola was asked for his reaction at Liverpool being paired with Bournemouth.

The 44-year-old replied (via liverpoolfc.com ): “Honestly, I was talking before the draw and I said, ‘The only team I don’t want is Bournemouth…’ For me, it’s special. They know me very well, they are playing very well lately, in a good moment, but it is what it is.

“We haven’t been very lucky with the draws – we have played Spurs and Chelsea already and now Bournemouth. That is going to be obviously special for me, but we have to earn the right to be in the semi-finals and I hope we can do it here at home again.”

articles.title: 'All The Emotions At Once': Inside The Brewers’ World-Series Winning Clubhouse
articles.summary: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Brewers center fielder Jackson Chourio, third baseman David Hamilton and right-handed reliever Abner Uribe stood side by side, put their arms around their shoulders and sang "Take Me Home, Country Roads" by John Denver.
body: As the World Series champions swayed and sang together in the clubhouse, Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers stood off to the side, grinning ear to ear, and watched his teammates celebrate the biggest accomplishment of their careers.

After Brewers closer Trevor Megill induced a ground out to Rays pinch-hitter Richie Palacios, and second baseman Brice Turang threw it to first, it was Bauers who secured the final out of Game 5 of the World Series to officially declare the 2026 Milwaukee Brewers first-time champions. The only thing running through his mind was that he needed to keep the ball safe.

"I’m so happy," Bauers told me in Milwaukee’s euphoric, beer-soaked clubhouse. "I’m so happy for my teammates. I’m so happy for the entire staff. I’m so happy for the city of Milwaukee. We did it together. I’ll keep saying that until I die. It’s true. We found something together, and we just kept going until it was over."
Bauers said he never wanted this to end. Winning 114 times this year was not enough.
